'''Raimond Bernard René Castaing''' (December 28, 1921 – April 10, 1998), also spelt as '''Raymond Castaing''', was a French solid state physicist and inventor of various materials characterization methods.<ref name=Wittry>{{Cite journal |last=Wittry |first=David B. |date=1992-04-01 |title=Remembrances of Raimond Castaing and his work |journal=Microscopy Microanalysis Microstructures |language=en |volume=3 |issue=2–3 |pages=XV–XVI |doi=10.1051/mmm:0199200302-30R1500 |issn=1154-2799|doi-access=free }}</ref> He was the founder of the French school of microanalysis and is referred to as the father of [[microanalysis]].<ref name=father>{{Cite journal |last=Colliex |first=Christian |date=2019-11-01 |title=The "father" of microanalysis: Raymond Castaing, creator of a generation of scientific instruments, still in worldwide operation |journal=Comptes Rendus Physique |series=La science en mouvement 2 : de 1940 aux premières années 1980 – Avancées en physique |language=en |volume=20 |issue=7 |pages=746–755 |doi=10.1016/j.crhy.2018.12.001 |bibcode=2019CRPhy..20..746C |issn=1631-0705|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Heinrich |first=Kurt F. J. |date=1998 |title=The Life and Achievements of Raymond Castaing |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/microscopy-and-microanalysis/article/abs/life-and-achievements-of-raymond-castaing/C8A6F7DB0938F91E88A976A02356B4A2 |journal=Microscopy and Microanalysis |language=en |volume=4 |issue=5 |page=517 |doi=10.1017/S1431927698210506 |bibcode=1998MiMic...4..517H |s2cid=137201147 |issn=1435-8115|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Castaing went to school in [[Monaco]], [[Condom, Gers|Condom]], and [[Toulouse]]. From 1940 he studied physics at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure in Paris]] (ENS) and at the [[University of Paris]], interrupted by work service in 1943/44. He also attended lectures by [[Frédéric Joliot-Curie]], who taught at the [[Collège de France]], and courses by [[Alfred Kastler]] and others at the ENS. In 1946 he graduated from the ENS and from 1947 he was an engineer with the national space research organization [[ONERA]]. In 1951 he received his doctorate under the supervision of [[André Guinier]], with the thesis titled ''Application des sondes électroniques à une méthode d'analyse ponctuelle chimique et cristallographique'' (Application of electron probes to local chemical and crystallographic analysis).<ref name=father /> He developed the microprobe named after him, which enabled material investigations in the micrometer range from the analysis of the X-ray spectra after electron bombardment (electron beam microanalysis, EPMA, Electron Probe Micro Analysis). In the late 1950s he was also involved in the development of [[secondary ion mass spectrometry]] (SIMS) (with his student [[Georges Slodzian]]).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Castaing |first1=Raimond |last2=Slodzian |first2=Georges |date=2021 |title=Microanalysis using secondary ion emission |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jms.4800 |journal=Journal of Mass Spectrometry |language=en |volume=56 |issue=12 |article-number=e4800 |doi=10.1002/jms.4800 |pmid=34935246 |s2cid=245083440 |issn=1076-5174|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Williams |first=P. |date=2011 |title=Raymond Castaing's Ion Microscope and Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry |journal=Microscopy and Microanalysis |language=en |volume=17 |issue=S2 |pages=562–563 |doi=10.1017/S1431927611003680 |bibcode=2011MiMic..17S.562W |issn=1435-8115|doi-access=free }}</ref> The first demonstration took place in 1960 and further development took place at the [[CAMECA|Cameca]] company and there was competition with the SIMS developed in the US by [[Richard Herzog]] and [[Helmut Liebl]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Castaing |first=R. |date=1967 |title=The early vicissitudes of electron probe x-ray microanalysis |journal=Physics Bulletin |volume=18 |issue=4 |pages=93–97|doi=10.1088/0031-9112/18/4/004 }}</ref> In 1952, he became a lecturer (''[[maître de conferences]]'') at the [[University of Toulouse]] and from 1956 at the [[University of Paris]]. From 1959 he was a professor at the [[University of Paris-Sud]] in [[Orsay]], where he founded the Laboratory for Solid State Physics with [[Jacques Friedel]] and others.<ref name=Roebling>{{Cite web |title=Presentation of the Roebling Medal of the Mineralogical Society of America for 1977 to Raimond Castaing |url=http://www.minsocam.org/ammin/AM63/AM63_601.pdf}}</ref><ref name=Wittry />

From 1968 to 1973 he was scientific director and later general director of ONERA. From 1982 he was on the French National Council for Reactor Safety Issues and from 1987 on the French National Committee for Nuclear Energy. In this capacity, he headed a state commission in 1996 that was to assess the [[Superphénix]] reactor. From 1984 to 1987 he was on the supervisory board of the French steel group [[Usinor]].

== Honors and awards ==
In 1966 he received the [[Fernand Holweck Medal and Prize|Holweck Prize]], in 1975 the [[CNRS Gold Medal]] and in 1977 the [[Roebling Medal]] of the [[Mineralogical Society of America]]. In 1968 he became a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|German Academy of Natural Scientists Leopoldina]]. In 1977 he also became a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Les membres du passé dont le nom commence par C {{!}} Liste des membres depuis la création de l'Académie des sciences {{!}} Membres {{!}} Nous connaître |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-depuis-la-creation-de-l-Academie-des-sciences/les-membres-du-passe-dont-le-nom-commence-par-c.html |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=www.academie-sciences.fr}}</ref><ref name=Roebling />
